messages.subject: Re: Decision tree creation metods
messages.body_plain:
Hi Peter,

There are quite a number of packages in R that can produce decision
trees, they are: rpart, party, Random Forests, rrp and tree (please let
me know if I have missed any).  At the moment, only rpart and Random
Forests are programmed into rattle.

It would be interesting to see "party" to be included as well.  "Party"
has a very strong statistical basis and a novel decision tree plot.

Another line you can go down is to use the rpart's custom split function
to implement some of latest Random Tree models.  Check out the
Extra-tree by Geurts et al. 2006, it is shown to be better than Random
Forests.

All the best,

Tony

messages.subject: Re: Decision tree creation metods
messages.body_plain:
Hi Peter, Tony,

Thanks for the comments.

Peter raises an issue I've been toying with - modularisation of
Rattle. This is a direction I hope Rattle will go, so that new modules
can more easily be added. I don't think it would be too hard to evolve
Rattles framework a little to support this in a much more rigorous
manner.

In recently adding the ada functionality, for example, most of the
functionality is in ada.R within Rattle, and this is "plugged in" to
rattle.R and rattle.glade. There is still a little too much in
rattle.R to support ada, but it is moving out. An extended Rattle GUI
would automatically add int the access to each new type of module as
it is added into Rattle. Each new module I've added to Rattle leads to
better clarity on how to modularise Rattle! But help is always
welcome.

I'll add party in the same way as ada (I've had a few requests for
party).

So feel free to add in new modules through a new xyz.R (with examples
of how to call the model builder to build a model, and how to call the
model to score new data)! I can certainly help plug it in, and as we
do, the framework will improve for doing this.

Would certainly be interesting to see Guerts' idea implemented.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: Rattle novice
messages.body_plain:
The "Data Mining Survival Guide" is a good place to start.

See: http://datamining.togaware.com/survivor/index.html

It is incomplete, but it does offer guidelines of how to proceed to load data and analyze it with Rattle. In a few places it mentions example data but I don't think there is a particular dataset that is carried through the whole thing.

This would be a good thing to have. Maybe we could grab one or two of the many data sets that come with R and build a tutorial around that. Maybe something like the Iris set would work? I don't know - I'm sure there's someone out there whose knowledge exceeds mine in this area.. I'm continually impressed by how many good datasets there are floating around the R universe
-Tom Arnodl

Thanks for pointing that out. It is actually now the audit dataset
that is distributed with Rattle. I've modified the section to reflect
this: http://datamining.togaware.com/survivor/Predicting_Fraud.html

In short:

library(rattle)
data(audit)
audit.rpart <- rpart(Adjusted ~ .,data=audit[,-12],parms=list(prior=c(.5,.5)))

Regards,
Graham
